hints: Apple counts are indistinguishable and children may receive zero apples.
Represent a distribution with n stars and m-1 separators.
Choose which m-1 positions among n+m-1 are separators.
analogy: Separators split one line of apples into m possibly empty shares.
correctness: Each separator placement uniquely determines the number of stars assigned to each child, including empty groups from adjacent separators or edges.
complexity: O(n+m) preprocessing and O(1) per case; O(n+m) space.
example: With n=3 children and m=2 apples, the six distributions are (0,0,2),(0,1,1),(0,2,0),(1,0,1),(1,1,0),(2,0,0). The count is C(4,2)=6.
algorithm: The number of ways to distribute m identical apples among n children is C(n+m-1,n-1). Precompute factorials and inverse factorials modulo 1,000,000,007, then evaluate the binomial coefficient.
